FORGEMCP — REAL-TIME HAND MOTION CAPTURE AND SKELETAL RETARGETING

Milestone ID: FMCP-BLENDER-WEBCAM-HAND-RETARGETING
Status: PROPOSED FUTURE WORK — NOT IMPLEMENTED
Depends on: A corrected, visually accepted hand rig and a documented rest-pose coordinate frame.

Concept

Use a local webcam and a continuous tracking process to estimate a person’s hand pose and retarget it to the Blender hand skeleton. MediaPipe Hand Landmarker may be evaluated as one candidate detector. The tracking loop must run in a suitable local process; an individual MCP request for every camera frame would add avoidable scheduling overhead and latency. MCP should manage bounded lifecycle/configuration operations such as start, inspect, stop and recording, while a local stream carries pose samples to Blender.

The current hand rig is only a prototype and bends fingers in the wrong direction. Webcam work must wait for anatomical correction. Camera tracking accuracy cannot compensate for a rig whose local axes and joint response are unresolved.

Proposed components

  1. Webcam acquisition with explicit camera selection, resolution, frame rate and permission state.
  2. Hand landmark detection with confidence values and timestamped frames.
  3. Handedness and pose estimation, including finger segment angles rather than only fingertip positions.
  4. Calibration between camera coordinates and the Blender hand’s rest-pose basis, scale and wrist location.
  5. Landmark-to-bone mapping for the wrist, palm, thumb and four digit chains.
  6. Coordinate-system conversion with an explicit test for handedness, axis signs and parent spaces.
  7. Joint rotation estimation with angle limits based on the corrected rig.
  8. Anatomical constraints to reduce impossible joint bends and discontinuities.
  9. Temporal smoothing with configurable latency and jitter bounds.
  10. Occlusion, low-confidence and tracking-loss handling, including safe hold or neutral fallback.
  11. Real-time pose delivery to Blender through a local process/channel, with bounded queues and stale-frame rejection.
  12. Live Blender visualization showing landmarks, bones, confidence and tracking status.
  13. Optional animation recording, including an explicit recording state and target Action.
  14. Keyframe generation from timestamped samples, with adjustable sampling and interpolation.
  15. Deterministic playback and comparison against recorded landmark input.
  16. Later Unreal Engine / Genesis Engine integration only after Blender-side behavior is accepted.

Proposed success measures

Set and publish thresholds before implementation. A reasonable first controlled target is stable operation at 30 camera frames per second; median capture-to-pose latency at or below 80 ms and 95th-percentile latency at or below 120 ms; at least 95% usable tracked frames during a defined 60-second unobstructed sequence; and median joint-angle error below 12 degrees against a labeled test sequence. After a short controlled occlusion, tracking should recover without a pose jump beyond the defined joint-rate limit. These are proposed acceptance targets, not present measurements.

Evaluate visible and partially occluded hands, varied skin tones and lighting, different hand sizes, left/right hands, camera placements and natural movement speeds. Report dropped frames, jitter, confidence, latency distributions and angle error separately. Require usable independent finger articulation, stable thumb opposition, consistent neutral calibration and a repeatable recording/playback round trip.

Staged research and safety boundaries

First compare candidate landmark detectors offline against a short annotated capture set. Then build a local tracker that can emit timestamped landmarks without controlling Blender. Next implement a Blender-side mapper against a corrected skeleton with a read-only preview mode. Only after numerical and visual review should live bone updates and optional recording be enabled.

No webcam tracking, MediaPipe integration, landmark loop, retargeter, live Blender drive, recording, or Unreal/Genesis integration was built as part of the October 30 hand-rig milestone. This record is a roadmap proposal only.
